translationRepairs: Datong 1, month 8, he slipped into besieged Lu; after defeat at Malaichuan the army abandoned Shangdang.
Dashun 1, month 8, he slipped into besieged Lu; after defeat at Malaichuan the army abandoned Shangdang.
Focus unit opens 大順元年八月; 大順 is the Tang Dashun era (not Datong 大同). Replacing Datong with Dashun corrects the era name without changing the rest of the sentence.

In the eighth month of Datong year 1 Jin commander besieged Lu prefecture; the Founder sent Congzhou with dare-death troops who by night held branches in their mouths and broke through the encirclement to enter; when the royal army was unfavorable at Malaichuan he then abandoned Shangdang and returned.

In the eighth month of Dashun year 1 Jin commander besieged Lu prefecture; the Founder sent Congzhou with dare-death troops who by night held branches in their mouths and broke through the encirclement to enter; when the royal army was unfavorable at Malaichuan he then abandoned Shangdang and returned.
Same Chinese date 大順元年八月; literal Datong is a wrong romanization of 大順. Dashun restores the correct era.
Datong he garrisoned Cao after Guo Shaobin took it.
Dashun he garrisoned Cao after Guo Shaobin took it.
Focus unit has 大順中; Datong misreads 大順. Dashun is the accurate era name while preserving the rest of the idiomatic compression.
In Datong, Guo Shaobin took Cao prefecture; Guiba led several thousand troops to guard it.
In Dashun, Guo Shaobin took Cao prefecture; Guiba led several thousand troops to guard it.
Literal likewise mistranslates 大順中 as Datong; Dashun matches the Chinese era.
Datong 1 he became honorary Minister of War and commanded the guard.
Dashun 1 he became honorary Minister of War and commanded the guard.
Focus unit begins 大順元年; Datong is incorrect for 大順. The proposed Dashun fix is accurate and otherwise leaves the sentence intact.
In Datong year 1 he was memorialized added honorary Minister of War and ordered to command the personal guard.
In Dashun year 1 he was memorialized added honorary Minister of War and ordered to command the personal guard.
Literal Datong year 1 misreads 大順元年; Dashun is the correct era romanization.
Xie Yanzhang came from Xu prefecture.
Chinese is 許州人, not 徐州; Xuzhou conventionally names 徐州. Xu prefecture correctly distinguishes 許州.
He defeated Qi Kerang at Rencheng and captured Lü Quanzhen.
He defeated Qi Kehu at Rencheng and captured Lü Quanzhen.
Chinese personal name is 齊克護; 護 is Kehu, not Kerang. The proposed name correction is required and otherwise preserves the sentence.
At that time Yanzhou's Qi Kerang had troops at Rencheng; Congzhou defeated him and captured his general Lü Quanzhen.
At that time Yanzhou's Qi Kehu had troops at Rencheng; Congzhou defeated him and captured his general Lü Quanzhen.
Same focus name 齊克護; literal Qi Kerang is a wrong reading of 護. Qi Kehu restores the correct personal name.
(The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Zhu Quanzhong urged return to Tang with Hu Zhen and Xie Tong.)〉
(The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Wen, seeing Chao's power daily wane and knowing he would fall, was urged by his trusted generals Hu Zhen and Xie Tong to return to the Tang state.)〉

Interlinear note has 親將胡真、謝瞳勸溫歸國: Hu Zhen and Xie Tong urge Wen. The prior idiomatic reverses agents (Zhu Quanzhong urging with them). The proposed wording restores the correct advisers-to-Wen direction and the omitted premise about Chao's decline.
(The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Zhu saw Chao's military power daily pinched, knew he would perish, and personally led Hu Zhen and Xie Tong to urge Zhu to return to the state.)〉
(The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Wen saw Chao's military power daily pinched, knew he would perish, and his trusted generals Hu Zhen and Xie Tong urged Wen to return to the state.)〉

親將 means trusted generals, not that Zhu personally led them; 勸溫歸國 makes Hu Zhen and Xie Tong the urgers. The prior literal invents agent reversal; the proposed after restores both 親將 and the urging direction.
He surrendered with Guiba and Guihou as guard officer.
At first he and his elder brothers Guiba and Guihou together gave allegiance to the Founder, and he was appointed a guard officer.

Chinese 始與兄歸霸、歸厚同歸於太祖，得署為牙校 states elder-brother kinship, joint allegiance to the Founder, and appointment as 牙校. The prior idiomatic drops 兄 and 太祖 and weakens 同歸 as mere surrender; the proposed after restores those facts accurately.
He handled frontier diplomacy for the early Xuanyi command.
When the Founder first held Xuanwu, he repeatedly ordered Guibian to knit good relations with the nearby borders, and he quite obtained the travelers' courtesy.

Chinese 宣武 is Xuanwu, not Xuanyi; the sentence also has 太祖初鎮 and named 歸弁 as ordered envoy. The prior idiomatic both misnames the command and omits the Founder/Guibian roles; the proposed after corrects the place and restores the missing agents.
When the Founder first held Xuanyi, he repeatedly ordered Guibian to knit good relations with near borders, quite obtaining travelers' courtesy.
When the Founder first held Xuanwu, he repeatedly ordered Guibian to knit good relations with near borders, quite obtaining travelers' courtesy.
Literal Xuanyi misromanizes 宣武; Xuanwu is the correct reading and the only change needed.
Guangqi at Neihuang he became honorary Minister of Works.
In Guangqi he again aided Zhang Cunjing in fighting Yan men at Neihuang; accumulating former and later merit, he was memorialized as honorary Minister of Works.

Chinese 又佐張存敬與燕人戰於內黃 records aiding Zhang Cunjing against Yan men at Neihuang before the honorary office. The prior idiomatic omits that aid and battle; the proposed after restores them without inventing content.
Datong at Yan he camped at Shanfu with Youliang and became Qi commander.

At the beginning of Dashun, when attacking Yan and Yun, he was ordered to aid Prince of Heng Youliang in camping at Shanfu; military prestige greatly shook, and he was soon made Qi prefecture commander.
大順初 is Dashun, not Datong; 攻討兗、鄆 names two prefectures (Yan and Yun), not a single Yan. The proposed after also restores aiding 衡王友諒 and the Qi prefecture command from the Chinese.
At the beginning of Datong attacking Yan and Yanzhou he was ordered to aid Prince of Heng Youliang to camp at Shanfu; military prestige greatly shook; soon he was Qi prefecture commander.
At the beginning of Dashun, attacking Yan and Yun, he was ordered to aid Prince of Heng Youliang to camp at Shanfu; military prestige greatly shook; soon he was Qi prefecture commander.
Literal Datong misreads 大順, and Yanzhou wrongly doubles 兗 for 鄆; Yun is the correct romanization of 鄆. Dashun plus Yan and Yun fixes both errors.
He executed Kang Wenshuang and three conspirators.
Kang Wenshuang and two others—three in all—wished to plot an outer response; he at once captured and executed them; popular hearts were then settled.

康文爽等三人 means Kang Wenshuang and others totaling three, not Kang plus three more. The prior idiomatic invents a four-person count; the proposed after restores the three-person total and the outer-response plot from the Chinese.
Winter month 11 he became Jin commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.
In the eleventh month of winter he was formally appointed Jin prefecture military commissioner and added honorary Director of Works.

Chinese adds 檢校司空; 司空 is Director/Minister of Works, not Grand Marshal (太尉). The proposal correctly fixes the title and expands the Jin appointment, but its English replacement embeds Chinese 司空; this revise keeps that English without the gloss.
In the eleventh month of winter he was formally appointed Jin prefecture military commissioner, added honorary Grand Marshal.
In the eleventh month of winter he was formally appointed Jin prefecture military commissioner, added honorary Director of Works.
Same office 檢校司空; literal honorary Grand Marshal is the wrong title for 司空. Director of Works is the accurate English office name.
He lifted the siege and became honorary Minister of Works.
When the army arrived it lifted the encirclement; he was added honorary Minister over the Masses.

Chinese adds 檢校司徒; 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Minister of Works. The proposal correctly restores the office and siege-lifting clause, but its English replacement embeds Chinese 司徒; this revise keeps that English without the gloss.
When the army arrived it lifted the encirclement; he was added honorary Minister of Works.
When the army arrived it lifted the encirclement; he was added honorary Minister over the Masses.
Literal likewise mislabels 司徒 as Minister of Works; Minister over the Masses is the correct title for 司徒.
